rule: Round 28 content for the W3 forms, each part behind its own switch: the letter-sound picker (listen, then tap one of five letters), four options for every story question, and the timed tasks continued past today's items to the end of the published lists. Built from published instruments only (src on every item); options written for this round are marked authored. Generated from the item-bank review sheet; never edit by hand.

sources.rwp2026: Rawalpindi/ICT May 2026 EGRA/EGMA (enumerator-administered, SurveyCTO codebook v109; N = 2,233, G1-5), fields cited per item
sources.egra_tk2009: RTI EGRA Toolkit (2009), English sample grids (familiar words p.30; letter grid p.24, which the Rawalpindi English letter grid adapts)
sources.core_egma: RTI Core EGMA (2013/2014), Student Stimuli Booklet: Sheet 1 number ID; Sheets 8-9 addition L1; Sheets 11-12 subtraction L1
sources.prpkp2020: Pakistan Reading Project 2020 KP endline, EGRA Urdu Form 1 (NORC report USAID DEC PA00Z7MW, form pages as page images)
sources.rti_rwanda2011: RTI Rwanda 2011 EGMA, P6 number identification (bank item-bank.sa-extra.v1.json maths.number_id_upper)
sources.tangerine_gh_sa: Tangerine SA-EGRMA Ghana form definitions (letters form: letter sounds; numbers form: number ID)
sources.jordan_egma_2021: Jordan Ministry of Education, EGMA 2021 Stimulus Sheets (RTI SharEd, PDF 11 May 2022), page A: Task 1 number identification, the child-facing grid (the 2021 Assessor Protocol p.1 prints a different, all 1-2 digit grid; the stimulus page is used)
sources.egra_tk2016: RTI EGRA Toolkit, 2nd edition (2016): the assessor rule that a regional or dialectal pronunciation of the word is correct
sources.pk_english: Mahboob & Ahmar (2004), "Pakistani English: phonology", in Schneider et al. (eds), A Handbook of Varieties of English, vol. 1; Rahman (1990), Pakistani English (the vowel and consonant patterns behind each accepted form)
sources.jordan_egma_2021_protocol: Jordan Ministry of Education, EGMA 2021 Assessor Protocol (RTI SharEd, PDF 11 May 2022), p.1: Task 1 number identification, the assessor grid (read left to right, line by line, as the protocol instructs)
sources.malawi_egma2010: Malawi Early Grade Mathematics Assessment (EGMA): National Baseline Report 2010 (MTPDS for USAID/Malawi, October 2011), Annex A Student Stimuli Booklet, Sheets 2(1)-2(2): number identification
sources.zambia_nas2014: Zambia Grade 2 National Assessment Survey 2014: Preliminary Mathematics Findings (RTI International), p.13: number identification items (the grid as printed)
sources.morocco_egma2012: Morocco EdData II: Student Performance in Reading and Mathematics, Pedagogic Practice, and School Management (RTI International, final report with instruments, 26 Apr 2012), Annex B EGMA Task 1, sheet 1M, grades 2-3, printed p.76 (read left to right, line by line, as the form instructs)

en.words4.rule: A local accent or regional pronunciation that keeps it the same word is correct; a change that makes a different word is not (come said as some, up as cup, find as fan stay wrong). The forms below are such local pronunciations, ruled word by word from the vowel and consonant patterns of English as spoken in Pakistan, each spelled as a speech-to-text engine writes it. Read by the scorer only; never shown or served.
en.words4.src: egra_tk2016 (the accent rule); pk_english (the patterns each form follows)
